boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on corridors adjoining or near NJIT, each with one documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Catch Newark Light Rail
cards.subtitle: Warren Street corridor — Warren Street and Lock Street
cards.notes: Use this station when your plan calls for Newark Light Rail; NJ TRANSIT lists it at Warren and Lock Streets with bike racks or lockers.
cards.short_summary: A documented rail stop at the campus edge.
cards.evidence_claim: NJ TRANSIT identifies Warren Street Light Rail Station at Warren Street and Lock Street, served by Newark Light Rail and equipped with bike racks or lockers.
cards.source_title: Warren Street Light Rail Station | NJ TRANSIT
cards.access_notes: Check NJ TRANSIT for current service and fare details before traveling.

cards.title: Pause at the landscaped plaza
cards.subtitle: Summit Street corridor — between Central Avenue and Bleeker Street
cards.notes: Meet or take a short outdoor break at the plaza; NJIT documents seating, benches, and paths joining the surrounding street entrances.
cards.short_summary: An NJIT-documented green-space plaza at a campus gateway.
cards.evidence_claim: NJIT describes Green at University Park as a landscaped plaza with a central seating area, benches, and paths connecting entrances at Bleeker/Summit and Central/MLK.
cards.source_title: Green at University Park | NJIT Campus Planning
cards.access_notes: Outdoor setting; use the street entrances identified by NJIT.

cards.title: Find a student-life hub
cards.subtitle: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard corridor — 350 MLK Jr. Blvd.
cards.notes: Check the public events calendar or gallery programming before heading over; Rutgers identifies the building as a gathering place for student life.
cards.short_summary: Rutgers–Newark’s campus center offers events, services, and gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers describes the Paul Robeson Campus Center as the center of student life and lists departments, programs, dining options, and services there.
cards.source_title: Paul Robeson Campus Center | Rutgers–Newark Events & Conference Services
cards.access_notes: Rutgers lists building hours; hours may vary during breaks, holidays, and special events.

cards.title: Use a nearby research library
cards.subtitle: University Avenue corridor — 185 University Avenue
cards.notes: Consult the current hours and visitor policies before going; the library is Rutgers–Newark’s intellectual hub with research and study resources.
cards.short_summary: A Rutgers–Newark library on University Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers University Libraries identifies John Cotton Dana Library at 185 University Avenue and describes it as a user-focused intellectual hub.
cards.source_title: Visit and Study in Newark | Rutgers University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Review current hours and visitor policies; some services and spaces may have eligibility rules.

cards.title: Spot Rutgers’ law and justice center
cards.subtitle: Washington Street corridor — 123 Washington Street
cards.notes: Look for public events or talks on the Rutgers calendar before visiting; the building houses Rutgers Law, its law library, and criminal justice.
cards.short_summary: A named Rutgers academic building with public-calendar events.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers identifies the Center for Law and Justice at 123 Washington Street as home to the School of Law–Newark, Law Library, and School of Criminal Justice.
cards.source_title: Center for Law and Justice | Rutgers Law School
cards.access_notes: Building access and event attendance can vary; confirm details with the event organizer.

cards.title: Plan an art-museum stop
cards.subtitle: Washington Street corridor — 49 Washington Street
cards.notes: Reserve tickets in advance and check exhibition details; the museum’s visitor page lists the Washington Street entrance and accessible facilities.
cards.short_summary: A downtown museum with advance-ticket guidance and accessible galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: The Newark Museum of Art lists its address as 49 Washington Street and states that guests must reserve tickets in advance; its galleries and levels are elevator accessible.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | The Newark Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Advance tickets are required; confirm admission terms and exhibition availability on the museum’s visit page.

cards.title: See the Philip Roth exhibition
cards.subtitle: Washington Street corridor — 5 Washington Street
cards.notes: Visit during library hours to see the Philip Roth exhibition, then use the accompanying audio tour; research-room access is by appointment.
cards.short_summary: A library stop with a public gallery exhibition.
cards.evidence_claim: The Newark Public Library’s Philip Roth exhibition page lists a public gallery at 5 Washington Street and says the exhibition is on view during regular library hours.
cards.source_title: Visit | On View at the Newark Public Library
cards.access_notes: The reading room is by appointment; verify current library and exhibition hours before departing.

cards.title: Visit the socially engaged arts center
cards.subtitle: Halsey Street corridor — 54 Halsey Street
cards.notes: Use the Halsey Street entrance and check studio or gallery schedules; Express Newark offers free admission and programs centered on making and art.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission Rutgers–Newark arts center in Hahne & Company.
cards.evidence_claim: Express Newark lists free admission at 54 Halsey Street and identifies itself as a center for socially engaged art with exhibitions, classes, and programs.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Saturday; gallery and studio hours vary, so check the relevant schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Use the downtown public square
cards.subtitle: Broad Street corridor — bounded by Broad Street, Park Place, and Rector Street
cards.notes: Check the park calendar, then explore its public art and monuments or attend a listed public program in this six-acre downtown park.
cards.short_summary: A six-acre downtown park with public art, monuments, and programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Newark City Parks Foundation describes Military Park as a six-acre park bounded by Broad Street, Park Place, and Rector Street, with monuments, public art, and public programs.
cards.source_title: Military Park | Newark City Parks Foundation
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space; consult the park calendar for scheduled programs and weather-related updates.

cards.title: Check the performance calendar
cards.subtitle: Center Street corridor — 1 Center Street
cards.notes: Choose a performance or education program from the current calendar, then review the venue’s directions and accessibility guidance before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: Newark’s performing-arts center at 1 Center Street.
cards.evidence_claim: NJPAC lists its location as 1 Center Street, Newark, and directs visitors to its event listings, directions, parking, and accessibility information.
cards.source_title: Visit NJPAC | New Jersey Performing Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Performance availability and ticket requirements vary by event; confirm details on the specific event page.
